requirements.name: ledger-cli-dispatch
requirements.text: Build a command-line cash ledger for a small shop. The product is an executable named `ledger` at the application root.

requirements.name: database-selection
requirements.text: `DATABASE_URL` names the database. When `DATABASE_URL` is unset, `DATABASE_PATH` is used, then `data/app.db`.

requirements.name: amount-cents-format
requirements.text: Amounts are stored as integer cents and never as floating point.

requirements.name: persistence-contract
requirements.text: All database access goes through the shipped persistence library and the relational layer generated from `DATABASE.md`. Application code never opens a database driver directly.

requirements.name: schema-init
requirements.text: `ledger init` drops all three tables if present and creates them empty. Nothing written.

requirements.name: schema-count
requirements.text: `ledger count` writes `table,rows`, then `accounts`, `categories`, `transactions` rows in that order.

requirements.name: csv-output
requirements.text: Every successful command except `init` writes CSV to standard output: one header row, then data rows, comma-separated, no quoting, no trailing spaces, `\n` line endings.

requirements.name: exit-codes
requirements.text:
| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Success. |
| `1` | Operational failure: database unreachable, tables missing, file unreadable. |
| `2` | Usage error: unknown command, unknown table or report, wrong argument count. |
| `3` | Rejected: invalid code, name, amount, date, or file row; duplicate key; unknown account or category; account in use; any change that would leave a negative balance. |
| `4` | Not found: `account get/rename/delete` of an absent account, `txn get/amend/delete` of an absent id. |

requirements.name: validate-code
requirements.text: Codes (`account`, `category`) are 1 to 12 characters from `A-Z` and `0-9`.

requirements.name: validate-text
requirements.text: Names and descriptions are 1 to 40 characters. Memos are 0 to 60 characters. None of them contains a comma or a newline.

requirements.name: validate-amount
requirements.text: Amounts on input match `-?DIGITS[.D[D]]`: at most two decimal places, never zero. On output an amount is written with exactly two decimal places, a leading `-` when negative, and no thousands separator: `-12.50`, `0.00`, `5000.00`.

requirements.name: validate-date
requirements.text: Dates are real calendar dates written `YYYY-MM-DD`. `2026-02-30` is rejected.

requirements.name: atomic-commands
requirements.text: Every command is one database transaction. A command that fails for any reason leaves every table exactly as it was. A load that rejects row 11 stores none of rows 1 to 10. A transfer stores both of its rows or neither.

requirements.name: nonnegative-balance
requirements.text: No command leaves an account balance below zero. An account's balance is the sum of its transaction amounts. Posting, amending, deleting, transferring, and loading are all subject to this rule, checked after the command's changes and before it commits.

requirements.name: load-accounts
requirements.text: `ledger load accounts <csv>` loads `accounts` from a file whose header matches the table's columns in the order above. Writes `table,loaded` and `accounts,<rows>`.

requirements.name: load-categories
requirements.text: `ledger load categories <csv>` loads `categories` from a file whose header matches the table's columns in the order above. Writes `table,loaded` and `categories,<rows>`.

requirements.name: load-transactions
requirements.text: `ledger load transactions <csv>` loads `transactions` from a file whose header matches the table's columns in the order above. A loaded transaction keeps the `txn_id` from its file. Writes `table,loaded` and `transactions,<rows>`.

requirements.name: reject-invalid-load
requirements.text: A load that rejects row 11 stores none of rows 1 to 10.

requirements.name: account-add
requirements.text: `ledger account add <code> <name>` writes the new account row.

requirements.name: account-get
requirements.text: `ledger account get <code>` writes the account row.

requirements.name: account-rename
requirements.text: `ledger account rename <code> <name>` writes the updated account row.

requirements.name: account-delete
requirements.text: `ledger account delete <code>` writes `deleted` and the code. Refused while the account has transactions.

requirements.name: txn-post
requirements.text: `ledger txn post <account> <category> <amount> <date> [<memo>]` writes the new transaction row. A posted transaction receives one more than the largest `txn_id` present, or `1` in an empty table.

requirements.name: txn-get
requirements.text: `ledger txn get <id>` writes the transaction row.

requirements.name: txn-amend
requirements.text: `ledger txn amend <id> <amount>` writes the updated transaction row. Only the amount changes.

requirements.name: txn-delete
requirements.text: `ledger txn delete <id>` writes `deleted` and the id.

requirements.name: transfer
requirements.text: `ledger transfer <from> <to> <amount> <date>` writes two transaction rows in category `TRANSFER`: `-amount` on `<from>` with memo `transfer to <to>`, then `+amount` on `<to>` with memo `transfer from <from>`. The amount is positive and the accounts differ. A transfer's outgoing row takes that id and its incoming row the next.

requirements.name: report-balances
requirements.text: `ledger report balances` writes `account,name,transactions,balance` per account ordered by code, then `TOTAL,,<count>,<sum>`.

requirements.name: report-categories
requirements.text: `ledger report categories` writes `category,description,transactions,inflow,outflow,net` per category ordered by code, including categories with no transactions, then `TOTAL,,<count>,<inflow>,<outflow>,<net>`. `inflow` is the sum of positive amounts. `outflow` is the sum of the absolute values of negative amounts, written as a positive number. `net` is `inflow - outflow`.

requirements.name: report-monthly
requirements.text: `ledger report monthly` writes `month,transactions,inflow,outflow,net` per `YYYY-MM` that has transactions, ascending, then `TOTAL,<count>,<inflow>,<outflow>,<net>`.

requirements.name: test-suite
requirements.text: The completed application provides a POSIX-compatible `bin/test.sh` that runs its own automated test suite from the application root and exits zero only when every test passes.

requirements.name: ledger-dispatch
requirements.text: The deliverable is an executable named ledger at the application root.

requirements.name: database-env
requirements.text: Database: DATABASE_URL when the caller sets it (for example a PostgreSQL DSN), otherwise a SQLite file in a fresh temporary directory.
